sentences.text:
Brajesh Sharma vs Aziz on 6 April, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Ind:8869
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Binod Kumar Dwivedi

On The 6 th Of April, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 1049 of 2017
 Brajesh Sharma
 Versus
 Aziz And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Santosh Pandey - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Pradip Kumar Gupta - Advocate for respondent No.3 / 
 Company.

Order 
This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 30/03/2017 passed by Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ujjain (M.P.) in Claim Case No.99/2016, whereby an amount of Rs.1,34,500/- has been awarded from the date of award to the appellant / injured with interest @ 6% per annum.

entities.text: Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ujjain
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is on lower side looking to the injuries suffered by the claimant.
Hence, prays that at least Rs.50,000/- more should have been given, which will be just and proper compensation.
On this ground learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount as prayed for.

3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.3 / Insurance Company opposed the prayer on the ground that amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the compensation NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8869 2 MA-1049-2017 amount.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.
From perusal of the record, it is apparent that claimant has suffered grievous injuries in the accident including the fracture below knee.

Even though the learned Claims Tribunal is not agree with the contention of the appellant that he has suffered permanent disability but looking to the nature of injuries, this Court is of the view that at least a lump sum amount of Rs.50,000/- should Brajesh Sharma vs Aziz on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157943037/
1 have been awarded over and above the amount already awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.

6. Therefore, without going into the nicety of the computation of the amount, the amount is enhanced and appellant / injured is entitled to an additional lump sum amount of Rs.50,000/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
7.
Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellant is allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.

Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation with interest to the appellant from the date of award i.e.
30/03/2017, which appears to be incorrect, therefore, the same is modified and it is directed that the appellant will be entitled for compensation with interest from the date of filing of claim petition.
Other terms and conditions of the impugned award including the interest part shall remain intact.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate.
(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Tej Brajesh Sharma vs Aziz on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157943037/
